# Requirements Quality Checklist: Update mode and destructive-operation guards

**Purpose**: Validate that every state the branch can be in has a stated, observable outcome, and that every operation capable of destroying or overwriting something a person wrote has both a stated guard and a stated default
**Created**: 2026-09-05
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## State Coverage — the branch's five states

- [x] CHK001 Is the outcome for a branch with no review request in any state stated as an outcome rather than implied by the absence of other rules? [Coverage, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK002 Is the outcome for exactly one open candidate stated without reference to what else may exist on the branch? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK003 Do FR-005 and FR-006 give a single answer for a branch carrying one open candidate **and** one or more merged or closed ones — is that "exactly one open" or "more than one candidate"? [Conflict, Spec §FR-005, §FR-006]
- [x] CHK004 Is the outcome specified for a branch whose only candidates are several closed ones, with none open? FR-008 addresses "a single closed candidate" and FR-006 addresses multiplicity, but neither names this combination. [Gap, Spec §FR-006, §FR-008]
- [x] CHK005 Is the outcome specified for a branch whose only candidates are several merged ones? [Gap, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK006 Is "candidate" defined precisely enough that a reader can decide membership without consulting an implementation? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK007 Is the ordering between pushing the branch and detecting candidates stated as a requirement, rather than only appearing in an edge-case bullet? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK008 Is any bound stated on how far back detection looks, or is detection over the branch's whole history on the forge intended and stated? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]

## Destructive Operations — guard and default

- [x] CHK009 Does every operation the feature can perform that overwrites text a person wrote have both a stated guard and a stated default? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014, §FR-016, §FR-017]
- [x] CHK010 Is the default for the description stated as a default, and is it distinguishable from the other two options being merely available? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK011 Is the set of operations exempted from a blanket skip-approval instruction complete — does it account for changing the target branch, which alters what the review request is against? [Gap, Spec §FR-020]
- [x] CHK012 Are the semantics of adding a reviewer stated in a way that cannot be satisfied by an operation that replaces the set with a superset? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016]
- [x] CHK013 Is removing a reviewer or assignee defined as reachable at all in update mode, or only prohibited as a side effect? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017]
- [x] CHK014 Is the requirement that a suppressed history rewrite be reported testable — does "what the user can do instead" name the alternatives, or leave them to the writer? [Measurability, Spec §FR-022]
- [x] CHK015 Is the behaviour specified when the description already contains two or more of the skill's begin markers, or a complete duplicate fence? FR-015a covers one marker without its partner only. [Gap, Spec §FR-015a]

## Approval Summary — completeness and measurability

- [x] CHK016 Is the set of fields the approval summary must cover enumerated, or is "every field it would change" left for the implementation to scope? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK017 Is it stated whether the summary must distinguish create mode from update mode to the reader? [Gap, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK018 Is "no field would change" defined against the same field set as FR-012, so the two cannot disagree? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, §FR-019]
- [x] CHK019 Is a requirement stated for values that went stale between being displayed and being approved — the edge case is listed but no requirement covers it? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK020 Are the requirements for a run where nothing changes complete — does FR-019 say whether the branch is still pushed or brought up to date? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019]

## Consistency Between Requirements and Success Criteria

- [x] CHK021 Does SC-002 hold for the merged case, where FR-009 requires a new review request to be created? Is "a run that reaches an update" defined? [Conflict, Spec §SC-002, §FR-009]
- [x] CHK022 Is SC-005 measurable without access to the forge's internal state — can "the branch's published history is identical" be established from the repository alone? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [x] CHK023 Is SC-006's claim that each of five states "reaches a stated outcome" checkable against the requirements, given CHK003 to CHK005 above? [Traceability, Spec §SC-006]
- [x] CHK024 Is SC-008 a user-facing or business outcome, or a repository housekeeping metric stated as a success criterion? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008]
- [x] CHK025 Is SC-007's "every behavioural claim" bounded enough to be checked, or does it require enumerating an open-ended set? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]

## Preservation and Scope Boundaries

- [x] CHK026 Is FR-030's "every existing guarantee this feature does not explicitly change" enumerable, or does the requirement depend on a list that exists only in the skills themselves? [Measurability, Spec §FR-030]
- [x] CHK027 Is the interaction between the existing draft question and FR-018 resolved — does the create-path question still appear in update mode, and if so does answering it count as the user asking? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-018]
- [x] CHK028 Is the interaction between the existing target-branch question and FR-018 resolved, given the edge case where the selected target differs from the existing review request's? [Conflict, Spec §FR-018, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK029 Is the permission edge case — able to create but not to edit — carried into a requirement, or does it stop at the edge-case list? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK030 Are the non-goals stated specifically enough to exclude adjacent work a reader might assume, particularly around merge options on an existing review request? [Clarity, Spec §Non-goals]

## Documentation and Rules Requirements

- [x] CHK031 Is "sufficient for a maintainer to check a claim" expressed as something a reviewer can decide, or does it require a judgment with no stated threshold? [Measurability, Spec §FR-025]
- [x] CHK032 Is FR-026's "the tool version each claim was verified against" stated per claim, per document, or per section? [Clarity, Spec §FR-026]
- [x] CHK033 Is FR-028's "load when the files they govern are opened" stated as an observable property rather than a mechanism? [Clarity, Spec §FR-028]
- [x] CHK034 Is the set of statements FR-029 requires correcting identified anywhere, or must the implementer discover it? [Traceability, Spec §FR-029]
- [x] CHK035 Do FR-025 and FR-027 together determine the document's structure sufficiently that two implementers would produce the same coverage? [Consistency, Spec §FR-025, §FR-027]

## Terminology

- [x] CHK036 Is "review request" used consistently for both forges' objects throughout, with the forge-specific names reserved for user-facing output? [Consistency, Spec §User Scenarios]
- [x] CHK037 Is "the branch's published history" defined once and used consistently, rather than alternating with rebasing or force-pushing vocabulary? [Consistency, Spec §FR-021, §FR-022]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- CHK003, CHK021 and CHK028 are the three items flagged as `[Conflict]`; each identified a place where two statements in the specification gave different answers to the same question, and each was resolved by amending the specification before planning
- All 37 items were evaluated against the amended specification on 2026-09-05 at the reviewer's explicit request, and every one is satisfied. The amendments the evaluation forced were: FR-005, FR-006, FR-008 and FR-009 rewritten so the state matrix is total; FR-010a, FR-012a, FR-012b, FR-018a and FR-020a added; FR-012 given an enumerated field set; FR-015a widened to a duplicated fence; FR-017, FR-018, FR-019, FR-020, FR-022, FR-025 through FR-029 and FR-030 tightened from judgment into checkable conditions; SC-002, SC-005, SC-006, SC-007 and SC-008 made measurable; a Non-goals subsection added
- Two of those amendments were defects the evaluation itself found rather than items in the list. SC-005 originally required the branch's remote tip to be unchanged, which the ordinary case of this feature — a user who amended the branch and re-ran — falsifies on every run; it now requires the previous tip to remain reachable, so commits may be added but none replaced. FR-018a stated a guard for the target branch without stating a default; the default is now the value the existing review request already holds
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
